problem:
The hyperbola ${x}^{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1$ intersects the line $x=1$ at

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $).$
worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=1,$ we substitute $x=1$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ (1)^{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ 1-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ -{y}^{2} & =0 \\ y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the vertical line $x=1$  at $(1,0).$
